messages:
mira: quick sync: we need to finalize the metric names/semantics for first-token latency and token throughput before I update the dashboard tiles and alert rules. I'm proposing a small taxonomy so dashboards + alerts share queries

alex: +1. taxonomy = good. what are you proposing for names? current variants in dashboards are a mess (FTT, TTFT, first_token_ms)

mira: yeah. proposal: canonical metric name = `redwood_infer_first_token_latency_ms` (gauge histogram). labels: `model`, `variant`, `region`, `deployment_type` (hosted/dedicated/private), `route`. Aggregations: p50/p95/p99 should be computed from histogram buckets.

jon: ok. what about the prefix vs suffix? I assume `_ms` is fine. For throughput, use `redwood_infer_tokens_per_sec` (counter measured per-request or derived?)

mira: good call. tokens/sec we'll derive from `redwood_infer_tokens_generated_total` (counter) and a rate() in dashboards/query layer. But we can expose a convenience recording rule `redwood_infer_tokens_per_sec` so it's easy to graph.

samir: for alerts, we should avoid sampling problems. Recommend using p95 over a 5m window for latency alerts, but for regression detection we should also keep a 1h p95. Example alert: p95 > 350ms over 5m AND p95_1h > baseline * 1.25?

mira: agree. We'll add two alert severities: P2 (5m p95 > 350ms) and P3 regression (1h p95 > baseline). Baseline will be per-model stored in config (not in metrics).

elaine: one nit: some models short-circuit and return very quick first tokens (quantized). We should include `quantization` label or `precision` label (e.g., fp16/int8) so dashboards can slice.

alex: +1 to `precision` label. Also we need to standardize units: ms for latency, tokens/sec for throughput. Dashboards should show p95 in ms and tok/s as a rate line with autoscale.

ops-bot: note: remind to add recording rules in prometheus namespace `redwood_infer:rules:v1` after agreement.

jon: example queries for Grafana (PromQL):

# p95 first-token latency over 5m per model
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_infer_first_token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, variant, region, precision))

# tokens/sec (recording rule will expose redwood_infer_tokens_per_sec)
# fallback raw derivation
rate(redwood_infer_tokens_generated_total[1m])

mira: perfect. also add `route` label to support different API paths (/v1/generate vs /v1/chat) so product can filter.

samir: will the histogram use ms buckets or seconds? use ms so small latencies have better resolution. Document bucket boundaries: [1,2,5,10,20,40,80,160,320,640,1280,2560] ms

mira: agreed. I'll add that to the metrics spec doc and create a short PR to the prometheus rules repo.

alex: can someone volunteer to review the PR and the dashboard changes? I can do the dashboard side (grafana panels + templating).

jon: I'll review the prometheus rules. Will also add tests to CI to check recording rule existence.

elaine: I'll check labels on model side (runtime exporter) to ensure `precision` and `route` get attached. Might need a tiny change in exporter code to plumb route through.

mira: thanks. action items: mira: update metrics spec + open PR; alex: dashboard panels + templating; jon: prometheus rules review + CI checks; elaine: exporter label changes; samir: write alert drafts. I'll ping in-thread when PRs are up.

alex: 👍 will wait for PR links

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled checkpoint at 1812353600 for rule rollout (automated).

mira: hooking regression alert to the new recording rules requires a follow-up — I'll include sample alert expressions in the PR, e.g.:

# P2 immediate latency alert (5m p95)
expr = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_infer_first_token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, variant, region, precision))
# alert when > 350
alert_expr: expr > 350

samir: fyi, for long-tail models we may want a lower threshold or model-specific overrides. we'll put overrides in the alert config as a map keyed by model name.

mira: good. filing the spec PR now, will drop links here once created. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

alex: :rocket:

jon: 👍
